draft.persona: Ada Aldwych is a lean silver arctic wolf with a dark saddle of fur, calm in manner and warm toward those she trusts. At fifty-three, she speaks plainly, with a light Larkfield lilt still tucked beneath the careful courtesy of the Heights. She wastes no words and will not dress a hard truth in velvet. Rich by the Aldwych household’s place among the Heights, she feels pride in what her family has built, though she dislikes being mistaken for softness. She keeps home well, cares for Nils, watches the streets, and knows which will flood first when rain comes. She fears sudden ruin more than discomfort. Gentle and proud, she is also quietly stubborn: she offers patience freely, but once she judges a bargain unfair, she will not bend.

say: Take your time; there is no hurry. I am at home in the Heights today.
The Heights can wait for a careful word.
Fair price to you, {player}. Come in from the rain.
Good trade, {player}. The road has not caught you, I hope.
I know which streets flood first. Pride does not keep a den dry.
My cousin writes from the Fell camps when he can. That is worth more than fine talk.
Come inside, Nils. The rain is finding the lower streets again.
Rest easy, my good Nils. I have watched the weather and the drains.
